README: This is a version of the Pite Saami lexical database in json format, including headwords with part of speech, grammatical information (consonant gradation, umlaut and stem extension patterns), syllable count and translations into English and Swedish, as well as additional entries which are word-forms (in which case the corresponding lemma is indicated) and phrases. Pite Saami is also known as Arjeplog Saami; the endonym is Bidumsáme giella; ISO-639-3: sje, glottocode: pite1240. The version, extraction date, license and contact information are listed in this json element; this is followed by desctiptions of the possible data types for the entries. Joshua Wilbur is the main editor, but the following individuals have also contributed to the collection: Nils-Henrik Bengtsson, Marianne Eriksson, Inger Fjällås, Eva-Karin Rosenberg, Gry Helen Sivertsen, Valborg Sjaggo, Dagny Skaile, Peter Steggo and Olve Utne.
contact: Joshua Wilbur, joshua.wilbur@ut.ee, Institute for Estonian and General Linguistics, University of Tartu
no: unique entry number from the source database
sje: Pite Saami entry (using Pite Saami orthography)
PoS: part of speech with possible values: [verb, adj (adjective), subst (noun), adv (adverb), konj (conjunction), egen (proper noun), post (postposition), pro (pronoun), dem (demonstrative), ptkl (particle), fråg (question word), num (numeral); fras (phrase), änd (suffix), utr (expression)] (NB: the final three values do not actually correspond to part of speech but are an entry type to classify entries from the origial source wordlist from the project Insamling av pitesamiska ord)
stemExt: stem extension pattern (includes the stem in case of a vowel alternation)
morphCats: morphological categories for entries which are not the citation form of the lexeme; more-less based on Swedish terms (e.g., ack for accustaive, komp for comparative) and Giellatekno standards (https://giellalt.uit.no/lang/sje/docu-sje-grammartags.html)
adjType: adjective type (attributive or predicative), with possible values: [ATTR, PRED, ATTR/PRED]
variant2headword: indicates the main variant if the current entry is not the main variant of the lemma
variantOfRefNo: indicates the entry number for the main variant of the lemma if the current entry is not the main variant
